recipes.name: Agua de Jamaica (Iced Hibiscus Tea)
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup chopped piloncillo (Mexican brown sugar cones)

steps.text: Place 6 cups of water in a large saucepan; bring to a boil. Stir in the hibiscus petals, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, and allspice. Reduce heat to medium-low, and gently simmer until the water has turned a deep red, 30 to 45 minutes.

Stir the chopped piloncillo into the hibiscus water until dissolved, then set aside to cool 15 minutes. After cooling, strain the warm liquid into a 1 gallon pitcher through a wire mesh strainer. Squeeze as much liquid from the petals as you can, then discard the petals. Stir in the white sugar until dissolved, then pour in enough cold water to fill the pitcher. Serve immediately or let stand overnight for best taste.

raw_recipe.headline: Agua de Jamaica (Iced Hibiscus Tea)
raw_recipe.description: Agua de Jamaica is a sweet, tart, and refreshing iced tea made with dried hibiscus flowers for a popular agua fresca drink throughout Mexico.

video.description: Quench your thirst with the vibrant flavors of homemade Agua de Jamaica, a refreshing Iced Hibiscus Tea! Join us in this step-by-step video tutorial as we guide you through the process of creating this traditional Mexican beverage. Learn the art of infusing hibiscus flowers, brewing the perfect tea, and crafting a delightful iced drink that's both flavorful and invigorating. Elevate your hydration game with this easy-to-follow recipe that brings a burst of tropical joy to every sip!

review.reviewBody:
AWESOME!! I don't have a gallon pitcher, so I halved the recipe, got a lil too much nutmeg (oops!) still delicious. Going to try to gradually reduce the sugar. Excellent recipe. Thank you SB!!
UPDATE: This has become my quaff du summer. In a 1/2 gl pitcher I've reduced the sugar to 1 medium cone of piloncillo and 1/2 c. white sugar. For some added goodness, I've squeezed a lime or two or three in it as well, so refreshing!

Good base, but hibiscus leaves are much too potent to be boiled only once. Repeat the straining process multiple times—a grease keeper helps immensely—and you can extend 1 cup of hibiscus to work for the full gallon of water. Tastes just like storebought.

The piloncillos make a very rich and earthy flavor in this tea! I did a full cup of piloncillos and one of white in a double batch. The spices are so aromatic my mouth is watering before I strained the tea and put it over ice. I garnished it with raspberries and a mini watermelon slice! Such a beautiful red! I used pure Hibiscus petals from our local Tienda Mexicana. Delicious and beautiful!
Absolutely delicious and refreshing! I only added 1/2 c of the sugar and it is delightful and tangy! The piloncillo adds a lovely flavor as well.

Wavered between 4 and 5 stars because the outcome was phenomenal, but I disagree with two things in the recipe: the amount of cold water to add at the end, and the amount of sugar needed. I'd suggest trying this with the same amount of hibiscus/spices/piloncillo, but instead of filling a gallon pitcher to the top, either fill it halfway or use a 1/2-gallon pitcher (2qt). Try it and see how you like it. Add more water if you think it needs watering down. The amount of white sugar can safely be halved and is plenty sweet at that point. Again, taste it and see what you think. Oh, and like others have said, add some lime juice when ready to drink!

There’s no way you need to boil this for 35 minutes. Just pour boiling water over the hibiscus petals. Also you don’t need this much sugar and white sugar, no. Use the piloncillo and agave or maple syrup Use cinnamon sticks or a few cinnamon spice tea bags if you don’t have all the spices.

I didn’t have Allspice but it turned out so good! It didn’t stain my pot or my countertop when I splashed some, but I wiped up immediately. It did stain the big plastic spoon I used. No biggie. I used a slotted spoon to fish out all the leaves and just pressed on side of pot. I only have a super small strainer, so it was much faster to just strain after I removed all the big stuff. Definitely will make again. I used much less sugar too, it had a great flavor already!

I brew the recipe and add a pinch of mulling spice lime juice fresh ginger and a cinnamon stick with sugar...which ever i have on hand...sometimes a blend...instead of pouring it into a gallon container i simmer and steep it until it resembles simple syrup and pour it into a fifth bottle...diluting and drinking some as well...this way it lasts a long time in the refrigerator and it can be customized for drinks either ice tea or mixed with spiced rum...even tried it with grand mariner both were very good and a little bit novel to the refined pallet. It is hands down a winner in my book.

Thanks for the added tips to lighten the tartness from the tea. I wanted to keep from using sugar at this point to maximize the benefit from the tea, its blood pressure lowering and diabetic properties. Ill add honey to taste.

After returning from our trip to Mexico, I wanted to keep Jamaica in our fridge for the summer. I don't use the white sugar and have experimented with varying amounts of piloncillo. The current batch is getting a tsp of orange flower water.

Oh my goodness, I am now completely addicted to this! The only changes I made are to use whole spices (obviously ground the nutmeg first!), and sadly, no sugar. I am using a stevia blend which suffices for me but it would the a thousand times more delicious with piloncillo. Thank you for this amazing recipe!
I made this drink took me a while to find the right taste with the sugar. But I finally got it just right if you do a gallon do half of the juice and half of water to even it out.
I come back to this recipe all the time because the spices compliment the hibiscus so well without overpowering it. I probably add half or less of the white sugar but that's to your taste.

I simmered for 45 minutes and most of the water was gone. I was left with only 1.5 cup. I added a gallon of water to it like it said. Tasted pretty watered down. I prob should just do 1/2 gallon. I could taste the tea which was good. Like most here I halved the sugar content and it was perfect for me.
First time making it with all the spices, I have to say I like it! From now on I will make it this way, I can't wait to try it with ice!!
From Sweden. Got the pedals from a friend travelling Mexico. Skipped the allspice and added one dried chili arbol. Switched to european sugar types. The best drink in the heat of the summer!!

My Mexican sister-in-law makes a much simpler version, but I LOVE the spices added to this one. Still experimenting to find the perfect amount of white sugar to add in addition to the piloncillo, and also whether I prefer lime or lemon juice as an addition to cut the sugar and perk it up. . However I make it, it’s always delicious! I’ve shared this recipe with a number of friends. Has anybody ever made a summer punch or cocktail using this as a base? Ideas?

Loved this drink! I felt the balance of spices to sweetness were perfect. I did not add as much water at the final step and left mine stronger, more like a punch than an infused water or light tea. My entire family could not get enough!
